```{r}
#| include: false
#| cache: false

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(readxl)
library(stringr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)
library(knitr)
library(scales)
library(here)

project_root <- normalizePath("..", mustWork = TRUE)

if (!file.exists(file.path(project_root, "DESCRIPTION"))) {
  stop(
    "DESCRIPTION not found at package root: ",
    project_root,
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

results_dir <- file.path(project_root, "results")
tables_dir <- file.path(results_dir, "tables")
figures_dir <- file.path(results_dir, "figures")

dir.create(tables_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(figures_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

devtools::load_all(project_root, quiet = TRUE)

if (!exists("ponte_calculate_qalys", mode = "function")) {
  stop(
    "`ponte_calculate_qalys()` was not loaded by devtools::load_all().",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

# Use at least 30 simulations before reporting simulation intervals.
n_simulations_main <- 1L
report_uncertainty <- n_simulations_main >= 30L

simulation_version <- "v_final_architecture_01"

sim_rds <- paste0(
  "module1_simulation_1998_2040_",
  simulation_version,
  "_nsim_",
  n_simulations_main,
  ".rds"
)

write_result_csv <- function(data, file_name) {
  readr::write_csv(data, file.path(tables_dir, file_name), na = "")
  invisible(data)
}

save_result_rds <- function(object, file_name) {
  saveRDS(object, file.path(results_dir, file_name))
  invisible(object)
}

weighted_sd <- function(x, w) {
  keep <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(w) & w > 0
  x <- x[keep]
  w <- w[keep]

  if (length(x) < 2L || sum(w) <= 0) return(NA_real_)

  mu <- weighted.mean(x, w)
  sqrt(sum(w * (x - mu)^2) / sum(w))
}

bmi_cat <- function(bmi) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(bmi)   ~ NA_character_,
    bmi < 18.5   ~ "underweight",
    bmi < 25.0   ~ "normal_weight",
    bmi < 30.0   ~ "overweight",
    bmi < 35.0   ~ "obesity_I",
    bmi < 40.0   ~ "obesity_II",
    TRUE         ~ "obesity_III"
  )
}
```

## Model Overview

The Portuguese implementation is delivered as the **PONTE-PT** R package:
an open-source, modular toolkit for annual dynamic microsimulation of adult
BMI trajectories, mortality, health-related quality of life, and
obesity-attributable economic outcomes. The package separates reusable model
logic from Portuguese parameter inputs, allowing adaptation to other
jurisdictions after local data replacement, calibration, and validation.

@fig-model-overview shows the framework's annual loop, Portugal-specific
inputs, and the three outcome modules.

### R Package Implementation

PONTE-PT is implemented as an R package and loaded from the local development
repository using `devtools::load_all()`. Core package functions prepare model
inputs, construct synthetic BMI cohorts, fit annual BMI-transition models,
initialise and update the simulated population, apply mortality, add entrant
cohorts, calculate QALYs, estimate obesity-attributable costs, and produce
validation diagnostics.

The analysis is reproducible through version-controlled source code, fixed
random seeds, structured input objects, automated output exports, and this
Quarto-based reporting workflow. This report uses the Portuguese parameter set;
the model logic is reusable, whereas population, BMI-transition, demographic,
mortality, utility, and cost inputs require local reassessment for transfer to
another setting.

The analysis was run with the development version of the PONTE-PT R package
(version `r packageVersion("pontept")`, accessed `r Sys.Date()`).

### Jurisdictional Transferability

The table below identifies which components are reusable and which require
local replacement when adapting PONTE-PT to another jurisdiction.

| Parameter group | Portuguese implementation | Requirement for another jurisdiction |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline population | NHS-based synthetic 1998 adult population | Replace with a local representative baseline population |
| BMI dynamics | Synthetic cohorts from Portuguese NHS waves | Re-estimate using local repeated cross-sectional or longitudinal data |
| Entrant cohorts | NHS donor pools and survey-weight targets | Replace with local entrant distributions and population targets |
| Mortality and demography | Portuguese life table and demographic inputs | Replace with local mortality and demographic data |
| Relative risks | Literature-derived BMI and education mortality RRs | Assess local applicability; use local estimates where possible |
| Utilities | Portuguese EQ-5D-5L age norms and external BMI decrements | Replace or reassess local valuation and utility evidence |
| Costs | Portuguese NHS 2018 direct-cost matrix | Replace with local payer-perspective costs and price year |
| Model logic | Annual individual updating and outcome aggregation | Reusable subject to structural-assumption review |
| Validation routines | Automated comparison framework | Reuse with local targets and predefined criteria |

---

## 1 Input Preparation

Model inputs were pre-processed before simulation and include the 1998 baseline population, repeated NHS BMI data, mortality life tables, entrant donor pools, and model settings. The analysis loads the prepared input object and validates the required components before simulation.

```{r}
#| label: prepare-inputs

prepared_inputs_file <- file.path(
  project_root,
  "data-raw",
  "model_inputs_prepared.rds"
)

prepare_script_file <- file.path(
  project_root,
  "data-raw",
  "prepare_model_inputs.R"
)

if (!file.exists(prepared_inputs_file)) {
  if (!file.exists(prepare_script_file)) {
    stop(
      "Neither prepared inputs nor preparation script were found:\n",
      prepared_inputs_file, "\n",
      prepare_script_file,
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  old_wd <- getwd()
  on.exit(setwd(old_wd), add = TRUE)
  setwd(project_root)

  source(prepare_script_file, local = new.env(parent = globalenv()))

  if (!file.exists(prepared_inputs_file)) {
    stop(
      "`prepare_model_inputs.R` completed but did not create:\n",
      prepared_inputs_file,
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
}

inputs <- readRDS(prepared_inputs_file)

required_input_names <- c(
  "population_1998",
  "bmi_panel",
  "life_table",
  "donor_pool_1998",
  "donor_pool_2005",
  "donor_pool_2014",
  "donor_pool_2019",
  "settings"
)

missing_inputs <- setdiff(required_input_names, names(inputs))

if (length(missing_inputs) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "Model inputs missing: ",
    paste(missing_inputs, collapse = ", "),
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

population_1998 <- inputs$population_1998
bmi_panel <- inputs$bmi_panel
life_table <- inputs$life_table
donor_pool_1998 <- inputs$donor_pool_1998
donor_pool_2005 <- inputs$donor_pool_2005
donor_pool_2014 <- inputs$donor_pool_2014
donor_pool_2019 <- inputs$donor_pool_2019
settings_base <- inputs$settings
```

```{r}
#| label: validate-donor-pools
#| include: false

donor_pools <- list(
  `1998` = donor_pool_1998,
  `2005` = donor_pool_2005,
  `2014` = donor_pool_2014,
  `2019` = donor_pool_2019
)

purrr::walk(
  donor_pools,
  \(pool) ponte_validate_entrant_donor_pool(donor_pool = pool)
)

donor_pool_sizes <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  donor_pools,
  \(pool, wave_year) tibble::tibble(
    wave_year = as.integer(wave_year),
    donor_records = nrow(pool),
    weighted_population = sum(pool$survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

write_result_csv(donor_pool_sizes, "module1_donor_pool_sizes.csv")
```

## 2 Derived Inputs

Three objects must be constructed before the simulation can run:

- **`rr_bmi`** — all-cause mortality relative risks by BMI category and sex, with normal weight as reference.
- **`rr_education`** — all-cause mortality relative risks by education level.
- **`bmi_transition_model`** — synthetic-cohort BMI-transition model fitted from the repeated NHS cross-sections.

```{r}
#| label: build-rr-bmi

rr_bmi <- tibble::tribble(
  ~sex,      ~bmi_category,    ~rr_bmi,
  "men",     "underweight",    1.85,
  "men",     "normal_weight",  1.00,
  "men",     "overweight",     0.94,
  "men",     "obesity_I",      1.12,
  "men",     "obesity_II",     1.42,
  "men",     "obesity_III",    1.92,
  "women",   "underweight",    1.82,
  "women",   "normal_weight",  1.00,
  "women",   "overweight",     0.97,
  "women",   "obesity_I",      1.09,
  "women",   "obesity_II",     1.38,
  "women",   "obesity_III",    1.85
)
```

```{r}
#| label: build-rr-education

# Mackenbach et al. (2024), Lancet Public Health.
# Lower education carries higher all-cause mortality risk.
rr_education <- tibble::tibble(
  education_level2 = c("lower", "higher"),
  rr_education = c(1.20, 0.90)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: build-bmi-model

bmi_panel_prepared <- ponte_prepare_bmi_panel(bmi_panel)

bmi_transitions <- ponte_build_bmi_synthetic_cohorts(
  bmi_panel_prepared
)

bmi_transition_model <- ponte_fit_bmi_transition(
  bmi_transitions,
  projection_period = 2014L
)
```

```{r}
#| label: validate-derived-inputs
#| include: false

ponte_validate_life_table(life_table)
ponte_validate_mortality_risks(
  rr_bmi = rr_bmi,
  rr_education = rr_education
)
```

## 3 Module 1: Obesity Trajectories 1998–2040

The simulation initialises in 1998 from the full NHS baseline population, aged 20–84 years. From 1999 onwards, new age-20 entrants are sampled from period-specific donor pools. Retrospective comparisons at the 2005, 2014, and 2019 NHS cross-sections are calibration diagnostics: they are not independent external validation because those data contribute to transition estimation and entrant-pool construction.

### 3.1 Simulation Settings

```{r}
#| label: settings-module1

settings_historical <- ponte_settings(
  initial_year = 1998L,
  projection_end_year = 2040L,
  entry_age = 20L,
  max_age = 84L,
  n_simulations = n_simulations_main,
  entrant_n_per_year = 100L,
  seed = 20260817L
)
```

### 3.2 Entrant Targets

New entrants are assigned the weighted NHS population size at age 20 for the survey wave closest to their entry year. The donor-wave allocation is 1998 for entry years 1999–2004, 2005 for 2005–2013, 2014 for 2014–2018, and 2019 for 2019–2040.

```{r}
#| label: entrant-targets-module1

entrant_by_wave <- bmi_panel |>
  filter(age == 20L, year %in% c(1998L, 2005L, 2014L, 2019L)) |>
  group_by(year, sex) |>
  summarise(
    entrant_population = sum(survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(wave_year = year)

entry_years <- seq.int(
  settings_historical$initial_year + 1L,
  settings_historical$projection_end_year
)

entrant_targets_historical <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  entry_year = entry_years,
  sex = c("men", "women")
) |>
  mutate(
    wave_year = case_when(
      entry_year <= 2004L ~ 1998L,
      entry_year <= 2013L ~ 2005L,
      entry_year <= 2018L ~ 2014L,
      TRUE ~ 2019L
    )
  ) |>
  left_join(entrant_by_wave, by = c("wave_year", "sex")) |>
  select(entry_year, sex, entrant_population) |>
  mutate(
    entry_year = as.integer(entry_year),
    entrant_population = as.numeric(entrant_population)
  ) |>
  arrange(entry_year, sex)

if (anyNA(entrant_targets_historical$entrant_population)) {
  stop(
    "Entrant targets are missing. Check bmi_panel includes age == 20 in all NHS waves.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

ponte_validate_entrant_targets(
  entrant_targets = entrant_targets_historical,
  start_year = settings_historical$initial_year + 1L,
  end_year = settings_historical$projection_end_year
)

write_result_csv(entrant_targets_historical, "module1_entrant_targets.csv")
```

### 3.3 Simulation

The result is stored as a versioned RDS file in `analysis/results/`. Increment `simulation_version` whenever model inputs, simulation logic, or model parameters that affect results are changed.

```{r}
#| label: run-module1
#| cache: false

donor_pools_module1 <- list(
  list(from = 1999L, to = 2004L, pool = donor_pool_1998),
  list(from = 2005L, to = 2013L, pool = donor_pool_2005),
  list(from = 2014L, to = 2018L, pool = donor_pool_2014),
  list(from = 2019L, to = 2040L, pool = donor_pool_2019)
)

sim_path <- file.path(results_dir, sim_rds)

if (file.exists(sim_path)) {
  simulation_historical <- readRDS(sim_path)

  cached_simulations <- dplyr::n_distinct(simulation_historical$simulation)
  if (cached_simulations != n_simulations_main) {
    stop(
      "Cached simulation has ", cached_simulations,
      " simulation(s), but n_simulations_main is ", n_simulations_main,
      ". Delete the stale cache or increment simulation_version.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
} else {
  simulation_historical <- ponte_run_simulation(
    population = population_1998,
    settings = settings_historical,
    life_table = life_table,
    rr_bmi = rr_bmi,
    rr_education = rr_education,
    donor_pool = donor_pool_1998,
    donor_pools = donor_pools_module1,
    entrant_targets = entrant_targets_historical,
    bmi_transition_model = bmi_transition_model,
    bmi_update_method = "legacy",
    stochastic_bmi = TRUE,
    education_source = "existing",
    bmi_limits = c(10, 80)
  )

  save_result_rds(simulation_historical, sim_rds)
  write_result_csv(
    simulation_historical,
    paste0("module1_simulation_1998_2040_", simulation_version, ".csv")
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: summarise-module1
#| include: false

historical_living_summary <- simulation_historical |>
  filter(alive) |>
  mutate(obesity = bmi >= 30) |>
  group_by(year, sex, education_level, simulation) |>
  summarise(
    mean_bmi = weighted.mean(bmi, w = survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    obesity_prevalence = weighted.mean(obesity, w = survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    weighted_population = sum(survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_records = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  group_by(year, sex, education_level) |>
  summarise(
    mean_bmi = mean(mean_bmi, na.rm = TRUE),
    obesity_prevalence = mean(obesity_prevalence, na.rm = TRUE),
    weighted_population = mean(weighted_population, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_records = mean(n_records, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(year, sex, education_level)

write_result_csv(
  historical_living_summary,
  "module1_living_population_summary.csv"
)
```

### 3.4 BMI Trajectory Summary

```{r}
#| label: tbl-module1-bmi
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Simulated mean BMI and obesity prevalence by sex and education level at selected years."

historical_living_summary |>
  filter(year %in% c(1998L, 2005L, 2014L, 2019L, 2030L, 2040L)) |>
  mutate(
    mean_bmi = round(mean_bmi, 2),
    obesity_prevalence = scales::percent(
      obesity_prevalence,
      accuracy = 0.1
    ),
    n_records = round(n_records)

  ) |>

    col.names = c(

      "Obesity prevalence", "Records (sim)"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-module1-obesity-trajectory
```

### 3.4a Mortality Input Consistency Check

> **Classification:** Internal consistency check / dependent calibration. The Portuguese life table is an input to the simulation, so this is not independent mortality validation. The comparison assesses whether simulated age-sex mortality is broadly consistent with life-table mortality after BMI and education relative-risk adjustments.

```{r}
#| label: mortality-consistency-check
#| include: false

age_breaks_mx <- c(20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 85)
age_labels_mx <- c("20–29", "30–39", "40–49", "50–59", "60–69", "70–79", "80–84")

lt_mx <- life_table |>
  mutate(
    mx_per1000 = -log1p(-qx) * 1000,
    age_band = cut(
      age,
      breaks = age_breaks_mx,
      right = FALSE,
      labels = age_labels_mx
    )
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(age_band)) |>
  group_by(sex, age_band) |>
  summarise(
    lt_mx_per1000 = mean(mx_per1000, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

sim_denom_1998 <- simulation_historical |>
  filter(year == 1998L, alive) |>
  mutate(
    age_band = cut(
      age,
      breaks = age_breaks_mx,
      right = FALSE,
      labels = age_labels_mx
    )
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(age_band)) |>
  group_by(sex, age_band) |>
  summarise(
    population_weight = sum(survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

sim_numer_1999 <- simulation_historical |>
  filter(year == 1999L, !alive) |>
  mutate(
    age_band = cut(
      age,
      breaks = age_breaks_mx,
      right = FALSE,
      labels = age_labels_mx
    )
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(age_band)) |>
  group_by(sex, age_band) |>
  summarise(
    death_weight = sum(survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

sim_mx_1998 <- sim_denom_1998 |>
  left_join(sim_numer_1999, by = c("sex", "age_band")) |>
  mutate(
    death_weight = replace_na(death_weight, 0),
    sim_mx_per1000 = 1000 * death_weight / population_weight
  )

mortality_consistency <- lt_mx |>
  left_join(sim_mx_1998, by = c("sex", "age_band")) |>
  mutate(
    mx_ratio = sim_mx_per1000 / lt_mx_per1000,
    mx_abs_diff = sim_mx_per1000 - lt_mx_per1000
  )

write_result_csv(
  mortality_consistency,
  "module1_mortality_consistency.csv"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-mortality-consistency
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Mortality input consistency: life-table central death rate versus simulated death rate for the 1998 exposure period, by sex and age group. Deaths recorded in 1999 arise from the 1998 to 1999 transition. Differences reflect relative-risk adjustment and stochastic variation."

mortality_consistency |>
  mutate(
    lt_mx_per1000 = round(lt_mx_per1000, 2),
    sim_mx_per1000 = round(sim_mx_per1000, 2),
    mx_ratio = round(mx_ratio, 3),
    mx_abs_diff = round(mx_abs_diff, 2)
  ) |>
  select(sex, age_band, lt_mx_per1000, sim_mx_per1000, mx_ratio, mx_abs_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Sex", "Age band", "Life-table mx / 1,000",
      "Simulated mx / 1,000", "Ratio (sim/LT)", "Absolute difference"
    )
  )
```

### 3.5 Retrospective Calibration

The simulated obesity prevalence is compared with observed NHS prevalence at the 2005, 2014, and 2019 survey waves. Because these waves contribute to parameter estimation and/or entrant pools, this is a dependent temporal calibration diagnostic, not independent validation.

```{r}
#| label: module1-validation
#| include: false

validation_years <- c(2005L, 2014L, 2019L)

observed_prevalence <- bmi_panel |>
  filter(year %in% validation_years) |>
  group_by(year, sex) |>
  summarise(
    obesity_prevalence_observed = weighted.mean(
      bmi >= 30,
      w = survey_weight,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    n_observed = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

simulated_prevalence <- simulation_historical |>
  filter(alive, year %in% validation_years) |>
  group_by(year, sex, simulation) |>
  summarise(
    obesity_prevalence = weighted.mean(
      bmi >= 30,
      w = survey_weight,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  group_by(year, sex) |>
  summarise(
    obesity_prevalence_simulated = mean(obesity_prevalence, na.rm = TRUE),
    sim_lo = if (report_uncertainty) {
      quantile(obesity_prevalence, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },
    sim_hi = if (report_uncertainty) {
      quantile(obesity_prevalence, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },
    n_simulations = n_distinct(simulation),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

validation_combined <- simulated_prevalence |>
  left_join(
    observed_prevalence |>
      select(year, sex, obesity_prevalence_observed, n_observed),
    by = c("year", "sex")
  ) |>
  arrange(year, sex)

validation_errors <- validation_combined |>
  mutate(
    signed_error = obesity_prevalence_simulated - obesity_prevalence_observed,
    absolute_error = abs(signed_error)
  )

mae <- mean(validation_errors$absolute_error, na.rm = TRUE)
rmse <- sqrt(mean(validation_errors$signed_error^2, na.rm = TRUE))

write_result_csv(
  validation_combined,
  "module1_validation_prevalence.csv"
)

write_result_csv(
  validation_errors,
  "module1_validation_errors.csv"
)
```

```{r}

#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Dependent temporal calibration: simulated and observed NHS obesity prevalence at survey years. Interval estimates are shown only when at least 30 simulation runs are available."

if (report_uncertainty) {
  validation_combined |>
    mutate(
      obesity_prevalence_simulated = scales::percent(
        obesity_prevalence_simulated,
        accuracy = 0.1
      ),
      sim_lo = scales::percent(sim_lo, accuracy = 0.1),
      sim_hi = scales::percent(sim_hi, accuracy = 0.1),

      )

      col.names = c("Year", "Sex", "Simulated", "Observed (NHS)")
    )
}
```

### 3.6 Calibration Error Metrics

```{r}
#| label: module1-error-metrics
#| echo: false

calibration_metrics <- tibble::tibble(
  metric = c("Mean absolute error", "Root mean squared error"),
  value = c(mae, rmse)
)

calibration_metrics |>
  mutate(value = scales::percent(value, accuracy = 0.01)) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Metric", "Value"))
```

Across the six sex-year comparisons, the model underestimates observed obesity
prevalence consistently, with a mean absolute error of 3.37 percentage points.
The directionally consistent negative bias indicates that the current BMI
transition specification does not fully reproduce the observed population-level
increase in obesity prevalence between 2005 and 2019. Because the NHS waves
inform transition estimation and entrant-pool construction, this result should
be interpreted as an internal calibration diagnostic rather than independent
validation.

## Module 2: Quality-adjusted Life Years

### 2.1 Population-weighted QALYs

QALYs are calculated for alive simulated individuals using age-specific
EQ-5D-5L utility norms for the Portuguese population [@Ferreira2023].
BMI-related utility decrements are applied to individuals with BMI at or
above 25 kg/m², using published estimates for overweight and obesity
[@OverweightUtilityReview2021].

No base-case utility decrement is applied to underweight BMI because the
selected decrement estimates apply to overweight and obesity categories only.


This module illustrates the framework’s ability to aggregate health-related
quality-of-life outcomes over time. The current implementation reports annual
population-weighted QALY totals for the living simulated population. These
totals reflect both population size and health-related quality of life; they
must not be interpreted as QALYs per person, education-specific QALY
inequalities, or externally validated estimates of disease burden.

The current implementation does not provide GBD-comparable years of life lost,
years lived with disability, or disability-adjusted life years. Those outcomes
would require a specified reference life table, cause-specific disability
weights, and external validation against appropriate Portuguese or GBD
estimates.

```{r}
#| label: run-module2-qalys
#| cache: false

qaly_results <- ponte_calculate_qalys(
  simulation_output = simulation_historical,
  min_age = 20L,
  max_age = 84L
)

if (!"by_year" %in% names(qaly_results)) {
  stop(
    "`ponte_calculate_qalys()` must return an object named `by_year`.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}


write_result_csv(
  qaly_results$by_year,
  "module2_qalys_by_year.csv"
)

if ("overall" %in% names(qaly_results)) {
  write_result_csv(
    qaly_results$overall,
    "module2_qalys_overall.csv"
  )
}

qaly_results_total <- qaly_results$by_year |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(
    total_qalys_weighted = sum(mean_total_qalys_weighted, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-module2-qalys-overall
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Annual total population-weighted QALYs accrued by the living simulated population, 1998–2040."

qaly_results_total |>
  summarise(
    mean_annual_total_qalys = mean(total_qalys_weighted, na.rm = TRUE),
    cumulative_total_qalys  = sum(total_qalys_weighted,  na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), \(x) round(x, 0))) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Mean annual total QALYs (weighted)",
      "Cumulative QALYs, 1998–2040 (weighted)"
    )
  )
```



## Module 3: Obesity-Attributable Economic Costs {#sec-module3}

> **Scope note — exploratory economic scenario, not externally validated cost modelling.**  
> Costs are derived from a published 2018 Portuguese baseline and scaled using
> simulated obesity prevalence. No independent comparison against another cost
> year or data source is performed here. Results should be described as an
> *internally consistent economic scenario driven by the microsimulation*, not
> as externally validated cost estimates.

Obesity-attributable direct medical costs are estimated from published
overweight-and-obesity direct medical costs for Portugal in 2018
[@Borges2025]. GBD 2019 BMI relative risks are used to derive obesity-only
population-attributable fractions (PAFs) for downstream disease groups.

Direct costs of obesity treatment are added at 100% attribution by definition.
Depression costs are retained as a descriptive published-cost category but are
excluded from the obesity-attributable total because GBD 2019 does not provide
a BMI-to-depression relative risk suitable for this PAF calculation.

### 3.1 GBD Relative Risks for PAF Derivation

```{r}
#| label: load-gbd-rr
#| include: false

gbd_rr_path <- file.path(
  project_root,
  "data-raw",
  "GBD_RR_2019",
  "gbd_rr_2019.xlsx"
)

if (!file.exists(gbd_rr_path)) {
  stop(
    "GBD relative-risk workbook not found at:\n",
    gbd_rr_path,
    "\nEnsure it is available in data-raw/GBD_RR_2019/.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

gbd_rr_matrix <- read_gbd_bmi_rr(path = gbd_rr_path)

rr_obesity_gbd <- transform_bmi_relative_risks(
  rr_matrix = gbd_rr_matrix,
  bmi_reference = 22,
  bmi_obesity = 32
)
```

### 3.2 Published 2018 Cost Inputs

Published costs are expressed in thousands of 2018 euros from the Portuguese
National Health Service perspective [@Borges2025].

```{r}
#| label: load-cost-inputs
#| include: false

costs_2018 <- obesity_direct_costs_2018()
pafs_ow_ob <- obesity_overweight_pafs()
cost_mapping <- obesity_cost_outcome_mapping()
published_prevalence_2018 <- obesity_prevalence_2018()

required_cost_columns <- c(
  "disease_group",
  "inpatient",
  "outpatient",
  "pharmacological",
  "total"
)

missing_cost_columns <- setdiff(
  required_cost_columns,
  names(costs_2018)
)

if (length(missing_cost_columns) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "`obesity_direct_costs_2018()` lacks required columns: ",
    paste(missing_cost_columns, collapse = ", "),
    call. = FALSE
  )
}
```

> **Note:** `published_prevalence_2018` is retained as a published comparator
> and audit input. The PAF calculation below uses simulated 2018 obesity
> prevalence to maintain internal consistency with the microsimulation.

### 3.3 Obesity-attributable Costs in 2018

```{r}
#| label: run-module3-costs
#| cache: false

exclude_groups <- c("obesity_overweight", "depression")

direct_obesity_costs <- costs_2018 |>
  filter(disease_group == "obesity_overweight")

depression_costs <- costs_2018 |>
  filter(disease_group == "depression")

costs_gbd <- costs_2018 |>
  filter(!disease_group %in% exclude_groups)

pafs_gbd <- pafs_ow_ob |>
  filter(!disease_group %in% exclude_groups)

if (nrow(direct_obesity_costs) != 1L) {
  stop(
    "Expected exactly one `obesity_overweight` cost row.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

if (nrow(depression_costs) != 1L) {
  stop(
    "Expected exactly one `depression` cost row.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

prevalence_2018_sim <- simulation_historical |>
  filter(alive, year == 2018L) |>
  group_by(sex) |>
  summarise(
    p_obesity = weighted.mean(
      bmi >= 30,
      w = survey_weight,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    sex = recode(
      sex,
      "men" = "Males",
      "women" = "Females"
    )
  )

if (nrow(prevalence_2018_sim) != 2L) {
  stop(
    "Expected simulated obesity prevalence for men and women in 2018.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

if (anyNA(prevalence_2018_sim$p_obesity)) {
  stop(
    "Simulated 2018 obesity prevalence contains missing values.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

obesity_costs <- calculate_obesity_costs(
  rr_obesity = rr_obesity_gbd,
  outcome_mapping = cost_mapping,
  prevalence = prevalence_2018_sim,
  costs_dro = costs_gbd,
  paf_ow_ob = pafs_gbd
)

required_cost_outputs <- c("costs_by_group", "paf_by_group", "total_costs")

missing_cost_outputs <- setdiff(
  required_cost_outputs,
  names(obesity_costs)
)

if (length(missing_cost_outputs) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "`calculate_obesity_costs()` is missing output(s): ",
    paste(missing_cost_outputs, collapse = ", "),
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

write_result_csv(
  prevalence_2018_sim,
  "module3_simulated_obesity_prevalence_2018.csv"
)

write_result_csv(
  obesity_costs$costs_by_group,
  "module3_obesity_costs_by_group_2018.csv"
)

write_result_csv(
  obesity_costs$paf_by_group,
  "module3_obesity_pafs_by_group_2018.csv"
)
```

```{r}

#| label: create-module3-combined-total
#| include: false

required_gbd_total_columns <- c(
  "inpatient_obesity_total",
  "outpatient_obesity_total",
  "pharmacological_obesity_total",
  "total_obesity"
)

missing_gbd_total_columns <- setdiff(
  required_gbd_total_columns,
  names(obesity_costs$total_costs)
)

if (length(missing_gbd_total_columns) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "`obesity_costs$total_costs` is missing: ",
    paste(missing_gbd_total_columns, collapse = ", "),
    ". Available columns: ",
    paste(names(obesity_costs$total_costs), collapse = ", "),
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

required_published_cost_columns <- c(
  "inpatient",
  "outpatient",
  "pharmacological",
  "total"
)

missing_published_cost_columns <- setdiff(
  required_published_cost_columns,
  names(direct_obesity_costs)
)

if (length(missing_published_cost_columns) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "`direct_obesity_costs` is missing: ",
    paste(missing_published_cost_columns, collapse = ", "),
    ". Available columns: ",
    paste(names(direct_obesity_costs), collapse = ", "),
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

gbd_cost_total <- obesity_costs$total_costs |>
  summarise(
    inpatient_k_eur = sum(inpatient_obesity_total, na.rm = TRUE),
    outpatient_k_eur = sum(outpatient_obesity_total, na.rm = TRUE),
    pharmacological_k_eur = sum(
      pharmacological_obesity_total,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    total_k_eur = sum(total_obesity, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

direct_obesity_total <- direct_obesity_costs |>
  summarise(
    inpatient_k_eur = sum(inpatient, na.rm = TRUE),
    outpatient_k_eur = sum(outpatient, na.rm = TRUE),
    pharmacological_k_eur = sum(pharmacological, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_k_eur = sum(total, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

cost_components <- bind_rows(
  gbd_cost_total |>
    mutate(component = "GBD-based downstream disease costs"),
  direct_obesity_total |>
    mutate(component = "Direct obesity-treatment costs")
)

combined_obesity_cost_total <- bind_rows(
  cost_components,
  cost_components |>
    summarise(
      component = "Combined obesity-attributable costs",
      inpatient_k_eur = sum(inpatient_k_eur, na.rm = TRUE),
      outpatient_k_eur = sum(outpatient_k_eur, na.rm = TRUE),
      pharmacological_k_eur = sum(pharmacological_k_eur, na.rm = TRUE),
      total_k_eur = sum(total_k_eur, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
) |>
  select(
    component,
    inpatient_k_eur,
    outpatient_k_eur,
    pharmacological_k_eur,
    total_k_eur
  )

write_result_csv(
  combined_obesity_cost_total,
  "module3_combined_obesity_cost_total_2018.csv"
)
```



```{r}
#| label: tbl-module3-special-groups
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Published cost groups handled outside the GBD-based PAF calculation. Direct obesity-treatment costs are included at 100% attribution. Depression costs are shown for context but excluded from the obesity-attributable total."

bind_rows(
  direct_obesity_costs |>
    mutate(
      treatment = "Included",
      note = "PAF = 1.0 by definition"
    ),
  depression_costs |>
    mutate(
      treatment = "Excluded",
      note = "No BMI-to-depression GBD relative risk"
    )
) |>
  select(
    disease_group,

  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Disease group",
      "Inpatient (k€)",
      "Outpatient (k€)",
      "Pharmacological (k€)",
      "Total (k€)",
      "Treatment",
      "Rationale"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-module3-total-costs
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Combined obesity-attributable direct medical costs in 2018. The combined total includes GBD-based downstream disease costs and direct obesity-treatment costs. Depression is excluded because no GBD BMI-to-depression relative risk was used."

combined_obesity_cost_total |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 0))) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Cost component",
      "Inpatient (k€)",
      "Outpatient (k€)",
      "Pharmacological (k€)",
      "Total (k€)"
    )

```

### 3.4 Interpretation and limitations

- The GBD relative-risk transformation evaluates the risk contrast at BMI 32 kg/m² relative to BMI 22 kg/m². It is a representative obesity-versus-reference scenario, not a continuous BMI-distribution PAF calculation.
- The published direct-cost matrix includes overweight-and-obesity costs, whereas downstream disease attribution is recalculated for obesity only. Do not interpret the resulting totals as directly comparable without this qualification.
- Direct treatment costs are included at full attribution because they represent the cost of treating obesity itself.
- Depression costs are excluded from the attributable total because no BMI-to-depression GBD relative risk is used in this analysis.
- The estimates are exploratory and internally consistent with the microsimulation; they have not been externally validated against another Portuguese cost year or administrative source.

### 3.5 Cost Trajectories, 2018–2040

Obesity-attributable direct medical costs are projected from the combined 2018
baseline by scaling annual costs in proportion to simulated obesity prevalence.
For each year, projected annual cost equals the combined 2018 baseline cost
multiplied by the ratio of simulated obesity prevalence in that year to
simulated obesity prevalence in 2018. Annual resource costs are reported in
constant 2018 euros and in inflation-adjusted 2026 euros. For economic
evaluation, costs after 2026 are additionally discounted to 2026 present value
at 3% per year.

The primary trajectory reports annual resource costs in constant 2018 euros
and inflation-adjusted 2026 euros. Discounted 2026-present-value costs are
reported separately in the accompanying table for economic-evaluation
purposes; they should not be interpreted as a projected annual healthcare
resource-burden trajectory.

```{r}
#| label: cost-trajectory-inputs
#| include: false

cpi_2026 <- 117.22
discount_rate <- 0.03

sim_prev_combined <- simulation_historical |>
  filter(alive, year >= 2018L, year <= 2040L) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(
    obesity_prev = weighted.mean(
      bmi >= 30,
      w = survey_weight,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

sim_prev_detail <- simulation_historical |>
  filter(alive, year >= 2018L, year <= 2040L) |>
  group_by(year, sex, education_level) |>
  summarise(
    obesity_prev = weighted.mean(
      bmi >= 30,
      w = survey_weight,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    population_weight = sum(survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

base_total_cost_2018 <- combined_obesity_cost_total |>
  filter(component == "Combined obesity-attributable costs") |>
  pull(total_k_eur)

if (length(base_total_cost_2018) != 1L || is.na(base_total_cost_2018)) {
  stop(
    "Expected exactly one combined 2018 baseline cost.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

prev_2018_sim <- sim_prev_combined |>
  filter(year == 2018L) |>
  pull(obesity_prev)

if (length(prev_2018_sim) != 1L ||
    is.na(prev_2018_sim) ||
    prev_2018_sim <= 0) {
  stop(
    "Simulated 2018 obesity prevalence must be one positive value.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: run-cost-trajectory
#| cache: false

cost_trajectory <- sim_prev_combined |>
  mutate(
    prevalence_scale = obesity_prev / prev_2018_sim,
    cost_constant_2018eur = base_total_cost_2018 * prevalence_scale,
    cost_2026eur_undiscounted = cost_constant_2018eur * (cpi_2026 / 100),
    discount_factor = if_else(
      year > 2026L,
      1 / ((1 + discount_rate) ^ (year - 2026L)),
      1
    ),
    cost_2026pv = cost_2026eur_undiscounted * discount_factor
  ) |>
  select(
    year,
    obesity_prev,
    prevalence_scale,
    discount_factor,
    cost_constant_2018eur,
    cost_2026eur_undiscounted,
    cost_2026pv
  )

write_result_csv(
  cost_trajectory,
  "module3_cost_trajectory_2018_2040.csv"
)

write_result_csv(
  sim_prev_detail,
  "module3_cost_prevalence_by_sex_education.csv"
)
```


```{r}
#| label: fig-cost-trajectory
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Projected annual obesity-attributable direct medical costs, 2018–2040. Costs are prevalence-scaled from the 2018 baseline and expressed in constant 2018 euros and 2026 euros. Both series represent annual resource costs and rise as simulated obesity prevalence increases."

cost_trajectory |>
  select(
    year,
    cost_constant_2018eur,
    cost_2026eur_undiscounted
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      cost_constant_2018eur,
      cost_2026eur_undiscounted
    ),
    names_to = "series",
    values_to = "cost_k_eur"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    series = recode(
      series,
      cost_constant_2018eur = "Annual resource cost (constant 2018€)",
      cost_2026eur_undiscounted = "Annual resource cost (2026€)"
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = cost_k_eur, linetype = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma_format()) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Annual cost (k€)",
    linetype = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```



```{r}
#| label: fig-cost-prevalence-trajectory
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Aggregate simulated obesity prevalence underlying the projected cost trajectory, 2018–2040. The dotted line marks the end of the NHS observation period."

sim_prev_combined |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = obesity_prev)) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 2019.5,
    linetype = "dotted",
    colour = "grey50"
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.0) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 0.1),
    limits = c(0, NA)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Obesity prevalence"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cost-trajectory
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Projected obesity-attributable direct medical costs, 2018–2040. Resource costs are shown in constant 2018 euros and as 2026-present-value costs after conversion to 2026 euros and discounting from 2027."

cost_trajectory |>
  mutate(
    obesity_prev = scales::percent(obesity_prev, accuracy = 0.1),
    prevalence_scale = round(prevalence_scale, 3),
    discount_factor = round(discount_factor, 3),
    cost_constant_2018eur = round(cost_constant_2018eur, 0),
    cost_2026eur_undiscounted = round(cost_2026eur_undiscounted, 0),
    cost_2026pv = round(cost_2026pv, 0)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Year",
      "Obesity prevalence",
      "Prevalence scale",
      "Discount factor",
      "Cost (constant 2018€, k)",
      "Cost (2026€, undiscounted, k)",
      "Cost (2026 PV, k)"
    )
  )
```
